alignments.note: Participle with a supplied subordinator (rule 86) and a supplied object *it* (rule 7), discontinuous under rule 15.
ὄχλοι → multitudes; the participle's subject is expressed, so the noun takes the English subject word under rule 74.
Verb with its subject and copula; rule 17 heads on the meaning-bearing predicate *afraid*.
Article before *God* with no English determiner (rule 23).

Second attributive article standing after the expressed head noun θεόν. Rule 31's test is whether the article governs an expressed head noun, and it names this very shape: `τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι` → *God who created* leaves the second article realizing nothing and gives *who* to the participle. Rule 90 is not available here, saying in terms that it blesses no unit in which a head noun is expressed, and rule 23 names a second attributive article as its own unrepresented unit.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; the relativizer and the auxiliary are rule 7/9 helpers on the participle under rule 31, headed on the lexical verb.
The ASV gives *men* no determiner, so the article anchors nothing (rules 21, 23).
Dative noun with the case preposition staying on it, no determiner having been written (rule 21).

review_notes: Corrected: s010 is the second article of τὸν θεὸν τὸν δόντα, standing after an expressed head noun, so rule 31 empties it and gives *who* to the participle. The accepted reading applied rule 90, which is scoped to a substantival article and expressly blesses no unit in which a head noun is expressed.
A reference comparison will report the unrepresented s010 as a disagreement; rule 32's closing clause says such a report is not a correction.
